findings.description: map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing any instance launched in this subnet (including aws_instance.portal_server) to automatically receive a public IP address, increasing exposure to untrusted networks.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, which will automatically assign public IPs to any instances placed in this subnet, expanding the network attack surface unnecessarily.
The EBS volume is created without setting encrypted = true (or a kms_key_id), so data stored on this attached disk is not encrypted at rest.

A default route (0.0.0.0/0) is created pointing to the internet gateway, which combined with public IP auto-assignment on both subnets exposes all instances in this route table to direct internet access.
AWS access key and secret key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata, console, or Terraform state.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.
The S3 bucket has no bucket policy, public access block, or ACL restrictions defined, and force_destroy is enabled, raising risk that flow log data could be publicly exposed or easily destroyed.

The snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk without any encryption settings visible here; if the source volume is not encrypted, this snapshot will also be unencrypted, exposing potentially sensitive disk data at rest and allowing it to be shared/copied without encryption enforcement.
